|strategy=By Michael Sharp, Gold 29<ref name="decipher-strategy">https://web.archive.org/web/20021114054040/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/small/darthvader.html</ref>

What more can you say? This is [[Darth Vader]], perhaps one of the most used and most loved Star Wars CCG cards.

With power of 6 he is definately a character of choice in battles, and also has the nice touch of adding +1 to EACH battle destiny draw. So now you don't need to worry about drawing that location that you know is coming up. All this and he's immune to attrition <5.

Combos:

[[Darth Vader{{!}}Vader]] + [[Grand Moff Tarkin{{!}}Tarkin]] - What an awesome combo! Power 10, a +1 to battle destiny draws, and the ability to cancel one of the Light Side's destiny draws!

[[Darth Vader{{!}}Vader]] + [[Grand Moff Tarkin{{!}}Tarkin]] + [[Vader's Cape]] (deployed on [[Grand Moff Tarkin{{!}}Tarkin]]) - POWER COMBO! Power 10, a +1 +1 to battle destiny draws, the ability to cancel one of the Light Side's destiny draws, and both are immune to attrition <5!
|rulings=* This card is a Black Squadron pilot.<ref name="scomp" />

Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020174249/https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json Internet Archive]</ref>

* [[Darth Vader]] + [[Force Field]] Cancels an attempt to target a Dark Jedi with a character weapon.

'''Virtual Modern Errata''' — [[Greedo (V) (Errata)]] (204_42) — current |sources=* Original printed face: [https://web.archive.org/web/20080512224452/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/anewhope/dark/small/greedo.html Greedo], [[Decipher]] (archived 12 May 2008). * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Dark Character: Greedo, A New Hope, R1 |strategy=By Tom Landyhttps://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/anewhope/dark/small/greedo.html [[Greedo]] isn't the greatest alien. In fact, nearly everybody says that his card isn't even worth space in a deck. But, in some cases, he can really be useful. At a deploy cost of one, this bounty hunter's power is two, his ability is one, his destiny is two, but his forfeit is only a half. [[Greedo]] also possesses a special ability which allows him to "threaten" Smugglers. His game text says: " During opponent's control phase, may "threaten" one smuggler at same site. Opponent may use all force pile cards to cancel "threat", allowing you to activate the same amount. Otherwise, draw destiny. If destiny plus [[Greedo]]'s ability is >6, smuggler is lost." Now I know what you are thinking. "Why would anyone use [[Greedo]]? His forfeit stinks, and to kill a smuggler, the destiny must be a six!" While all of this is true, there are always ways to improve things. For instance, to improve his forfeit, keep him around the dark side's [[Tatooine: Mos Eisley (Dark){{!}}Tatooine: Mos Eisley]]. Here, [[Greedo]]'s forfeit would get a plus one bonus, and his power would be three. Another quick way to boost his forfeit is to slap a [[Stormtrooper Utility Belt]] around his waist. [[Greedo]]'s forfeit and power would both get a plus one bonus, but if he was on the [[Death Star]], the bonus would be plus two. Now, a forfeit of two and a half isn't bad. If you have a lot of destinies of six in your deck, you will be able to "threaten" major smugglers like [[Han Solo{{!}}Han]], [[Chewbacca]], and even [[Wedge Antilles]] easily if you have certain cards that will help you. An [[Electrobinoculars]] would be ideal to locate destinies of six, if only the dark side had this device. So, use [[Reegesk]], [[Tonnika Sisters]] or any other way to steal them from your opponent. [[Electrobinoculars]] is a very popular and powerful card, so you don't have to really worry about your opponent not having them. Another good way to find destinies that you need is with [[R2-Q2 (Artoo-Kyootoo){{!}}R2-Q2]]. When at a scomp link, [[R2-Q2 (Artoo-Kyootoo){{!}}R2-Q2]] enables you to peek at the top three cards of your reserve deck during your draw phase for one force. By knowing what your destiny is, even if it isn't a six, you can still bluff because your opponent won't know if you are lying or not. [[Greedo]]'s forfeit value and special ability to "threaten" smugglers aren't great, but when combined with certain cards it can really be helpful. |pulled_by=* [[Double Back]]Lookup: [https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Greedo Scomp: Greedo]. [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/d4e661ec735dcb111266fbda98704f2181e1cfab/Dark.json swccg-card-json Dark.json], Players Committee, Greedo (GEMP ID 2_89, commit d4e661ec735dcb111266fbda98704f2181e1cfab), pulledBy record supporting Double Back. '''Decipher (Revised)''' — [[General Veers (Revised)]] (53_87) |sources=* [[Media:Decipher_Glossary_1998.pdf|Decipher Glossary Version 2.0]] (November 1998) * Printed face: [[General Veers]] |strategy=By Gregg Keefer, Gold 4https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/hoth/dark/small/generalveers.html [[General Veers]] is one bad dude. How many people out there can face [[Darth Vader]], nose to breathing apparatus, without flinching? Aside from hispersonal charm and charisma his card is stacked with tons of useful abilitiesthat will add to your Dark Side deck and make those rebels quake with fear! For 3 Force you get 3 power and 3 ability as well as [[Red Leader{{!}}Leader]] ability. Add to that the fact that he is a Warrior and a Pilot and you have a useful, do-it-all character that works well in practically any deck strategy. But that's notall, this guy is the bomb. His pilot text carries added bonuses if you use him on combat vehicles. He adds 3 to the power of any combat vehicle which can make any Walker a nightmare to be reckoned with. Put him on the [[Imperial Walker]] from the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] 2 player game[, with its permanent pilot of ability 1, and you have 7 power and a battle destiny draw for only 7 Force. Put him on [[Blizzard 1]] and [[Veers]] commands a staggering 10 power, immunity to attrition less than 4 and a battle destiny draw all by himself ! The mighty General also adds 1 to armor on this Walker making it that much harder for those pesky Snowspeeders to take him down with their puny weapons. Bah, annoying gadflies! He's great on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] but he can really make trouble for those rebels at Cloud Sectors too. Put him on a [[Cloud Car (Dark){{!}}Cloud Car]] (a combat vehicle) at a Cloud Sector and you are looking at 6 power and a battle destiny draw for only 5 Force. Combine this with some Tibanna Gas Miners on the ground to add to your Force drain at the sector. If it's a Light Side cloud sector you're controlling you'll drain for 2, plus the Miner bonus. Nasty. He's also power plus one at the same site as that bumbling freebie [[Admiral Ozzel]] and they'll bring you 7 power (8 on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]]) plus a battle destiny for only 3 Force. Ozzel was born to be forfeited to attrition, leaving [[Veers]] to fight again another day. Should the unthinkable happen and [[Veers]] is defeated, his better than average forfeit of 5 will usually eat up even a high single destiny in attrition. General Maximillian [[Veers]]' great abilities have won him the admiration of the Empire. He is yours to command. The shield generators will be down in moments, you may start your landing. |pulled_by=* [[Blizzard 4]][https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=General%20Veers Scomp: General Veers]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). Immune to attrition < 4. |errata_history=Versions of [[Boba Fett (V)]] in [[Virtual Set 6: City In The Clouds]], in date order (3 versions). Slip texts are quoted as printed: ▼ and ▲ are the slips' arrow icons (deploy from / take into hand from Reserve Deck; reshuffle), and the immunity and pilot icons are the ones explained in each sheet's icon key (see [[Virtual card icons]]). Found while adding the original pre-Remaster slips (Bill, 12 November 2026). * '''Original''' ([[Boba Fett (V) (Virtual Set 6)]]): the Committee's interim rules supplement “Star Wars CCG Changes to Virtual Set #6” (“Updated 31 Dec 2003”; PDF dated 31 December 2003; [https://web.archive.org/web/20040615005231/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Resources/v6changes.pdf v6changes.pdf on swccgpc.com], Internet Archive capture of 15 June 2004), Section 2. Updated Dark Side Texts, lists the card with only this line: “This virtual card must be used with the Cloud City set persona.” It gives no game text, stats or lore; the supplement is “an official rules document” giving “interim updated card text” and says the texts “are not final and may differ from the texts provided in the final version of Virtual Set #6”. Stats and lore on this page are those of the January 2004 slip. This is the earliest surviving publication of the card: the first release sheet of 21 November 2003 is not preserved. Image: the card's entry cut from the supplement ([[:File:OVS6-29-Boba_Fett-interim-text-2003-12-31.png]]). * '''PC-E1''' ([[Boba Fett (V) (Virtual Set 6) (Errata)]]): the “Final Revised Virtual Set 6” sheet “Virtual Set #6” (Players Committee; announced and tournament-legal 12 January 2004; PDF dated 12 January 2004), page 2, slip 29 — [https://web.archive.org/web/20040619231451/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Resources/AbsolutelyFinalVersion6.pdf AbsolutelyFinalVersion6.pdf on swccgpc.com] (Internet Archive capture of 19 June 2004; the Committee still hosts the same file as [https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualCards6.pdf VirtualCards6.pdf] on res.starwarsccg.org), announced on the [https://web.archive.org/web/20040415220046/http://swccgpc.com/interior.htm Committee's news page]: “P 3. Once during your control phase, may ▲ any card with 'Bounty' in title. Your cards with 'Bounty' in the title are immune to Aim High. May “fly” (landspeed = 3). Draws one battle destiny if unable to otherwise. Immune to attrition < 4.” The first release sheet of 21 November 2003 is not preserved. Stats line: “POWER 4 ABILITY 3 ARMOR 5”. Deploy 4, forfeit 7. The slip is the old pre-template slip the Committee used before its December 2006 Remaster: the Decipher-style lower half with the slip mark “6•29” at bottom right and no expansion icon. The updated sheet of 12 October 2004 ([https://web.archive.org/web/20050406053829/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Resources/Virtual%20Set%206.pdf Virtual Set 6.pdf], Internet Archive 6 April 2005; PDF dated 12 October 2004) prints the same words on the same old slip ([[:File:OVS6-29-Boba_Fett-original-slip-2004-10-12.png]]). '''What changed''' (from the 31 December 2003 interim text): the slip gives the card's full game text, stats and lore (“P 3. Once during your control phase, may ▲ any card with 'Bounty' in title. …”); the supplement gave no game text, only the persona note. * '''PC-E2''' (this page): the Remaster sheet (official text as of 4 December 2006; [https://web.archive.org/web/20071024154341/http://www.swccgpc.com/Resources/VirtualCards6.pdf Internet Archive capture of 24 October 2007], slip 29), in the Committee's Remaster template: “Adds 3 to power of anything he pilots. May ‘fly’ (landspeed = 3). Draws one battle destiny if unable to otherwise. Your cards with “Bounty” in title are immune to Aim High. During your control phase, may take a card with “Bounty” in title into hand from Reserve Deck; reshuffle. Immune to attrition < 4.” '''What changed:''' the Remaster rewrote the slip in the Committee's later wording (full text above; icons written out in words here). This is the current text of the Virtual Original card. |printings='''Decipher''' — [[Boba Fett (Cloud City)]] (5_91o)

'''Decipher (Revised)''' — [[General Veers (Revised)]] (53_87) |sources=* [[Media:Decipher_Glossary_1998.pdf|Decipher Glossary Version 2.0]] (General Veers; November 1998) * Printed face: [[General Veers]] |strategy=By Gregg Keefer, Gold 4https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/hoth/dark/small/generalveers.html [[General Veers]] is one bad dude. How many people out there can face [[Darth Vader]], nose to breathing apparatus, without flinching? Aside from hispersonal charm and charisma his card is stacked with tons of useful abilitiesthat will add to your Dark Side deck and make those rebels quake with fear! For 3 Force you get 3 power and 3 ability as well as [[Red Leader{{!}}Leader]] ability. Add to that the fact that he is a Warrior and a Pilot and you have a useful, do-it-all character that works well in practically any deck strategy. But that's notall, this guy is the bomb. His pilot text carries added bonuses if you use him on combat vehicles. He adds 3 to the power of any combat vehicle which can make any Walker a nightmare to be reckoned with. Put him on the [[Imperial Walker]] from the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] 2 player game[, with its permanent pilot of ability 1, and you have 7 power and a battle destiny draw for only 7 Force. Put him on [[Blizzard 1]] and [[Veers]] commands a staggering 10 power, immunity to attrition less than 4 and a battle destiny draw all by himself ! The mighty General also adds 1 to armor on this Walker making it that much harder for those pesky Snowspeeders to take him down with their puny weapons. Bah, annoying gadflies! He's great on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] but he can really make trouble for those rebels at Cloud Sectors too. Put him on a [[Cloud Car (Dark){{!}}Cloud Car]] (a combat vehicle) at a Cloud Sector and you are looking at 6 power and a battle destiny draw for only 5 Force. Combine this with some Tibanna Gas Miners on the ground to add to your Force drain at the sector. If it's a Light Side cloud sector you're controlling you'll drain for 2, plus the Miner bonus. Nasty. He's also power plus one at the same site as that bumbling freebie [[Admiral Ozzel]] and they'll bring you 7 power (8 on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]]) plus a battle destiny for only 3 Force. Ozzel was born to be forfeited to attrition, leaving [[Veers]] to fight again another day. Should the unthinkable happen and [[Veers]] is defeated, his better than average forfeit of 5 will usually eat up even a high single destiny in attrition. {{Set infobox |name=Premiere (Japanese) |image=Premiere-Japanese-box.png |publisher=[[Decipher]] / [[Takara]] |era=[[:Category:Decipher sets|Decipher]] (1995–2001) |released=April 1997 |cards=324 (162 Light, 162 Dark) |code=GEMP set 1301 |country=Japan |language=Japanese |next=[[A New Hope (Japanese)]] |related=[[Premiere Limited]] · [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] }} '''Premiere (Japanese)''' (基本カード) is the Japanese-language edition of [[Premiere Limited]]. [[Takara]] published it in Japan in April 1997 as スターウォーズコレクションカードゲーム. It has 324 black-border cards, 162 Light Side and 162 Dark Side, 108 of each rarity. Decipher and Takara announced the partnership in December 1996. Steve Stanley, Decipher Senior Vice President and General Counsel, visited Tokyo for Takara's introduction of the set. Takara demonstrated it at the Tokyo Toy Show, 19–23 March 1997, at Tokyo Big Sight. The first three days were trade only. The last two days were open to the public. Takara's gameplay demonstrations had standing room only. Hirohisa Satoh, Jr., President of Takara Ltd., hosted the display. Takara pre-sold more than 80 percent of the print run before street date. Takara was translating the Tournament Kit. Japan was placed in the newly created Ord Mantell region on Decipher's tournament locator. A Japanese champion was expected to compete at the [[1997 Decipher World Championship]]. Takara could not ship the Japanese cards outside Japan. The English Limited set is the 1st expansion of Star Wars CCG. This printing translates that 324-card pool. GEMP loads the Japanese faces as set 1301. English-language packs from [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] through [[Endor]] were sold in Japan with a Takara overlabel on the pack. Poor translations led Japanese players to prefer the English-language cards. Takara and Decipher ended the partnership after Japanese Premiere, [[A New Hope (Japanese)|A New Hope]], [[Hoth (Japanese)|Hoth]], and the two Japanese two-player games. [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] has a separate Japanese product. Language editions are listed on [[Translations of SWCCG]]. == Packaging == Takara sold 15-card booster packs (MSRP ¥500) in 36-pack boxes. Each pack had 10 commons, 4 uncommons and 1 rare. 60-card starters (MSRP ¥1400) came in 12-deck displays. Each starter had 44 commons (22 per side), 14 uncommons (7 per side), 2 rares (1 per side) and a Japanese rulebook. {| class="wikitable" style="background:transparent; border:none;" |- style="background:transparent; border:none; vertical-align:bottom;" | style="border:none; text-align:center;" | [[File:Premiere-Japanese-box.png|260px|Japanese booster box]]

There was no corrected run, so it is not counted as a separate misprint. The mark is part of the print-sheet layout. [[File:Premiere-Japanese-Corellian-Corvette-title-mark-v2.png|480px|Japanese Corellian Corvette title mark]] ''[[Corellian Corvette (Japanese)|Corellian Corvette]]: unmarked title and print-sheet mark'' == Other printings == English-language packs from [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] through [[Endor]] were sold in Japan with a Takara overlabel on the pack. [[File:Premiere-Japanese-Takara-overlabel-packs.png|520px|Takara overlabels on English A New Hope and Dagobah packs]] ''English [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]] and [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] packs with Takara overlabels'' The English edition is [[Premiere Limited]]. The Japanese [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] followed in 1997. Japanese-language foil versions of some Premiere cards were packed in [[Reflections II: Expanding the Galaxy]] and [[Reflections III]]. They belong to those English products. {{Card |title=Greedo (Revised) |versions='''Decipher''' — [[Greedo]] (2_89)
'''Decipher (Revised)''' — '''this page''' (52_89) |gemp_id=52_89 |card_uid=52_89 |image=ANH-R-D-greedowb.gif |side=Dark |type=Character |subtype=Alien |subtype_link=Alien |set=Revised A New Hope |publisher=[[Decipher]] |era=[[Decipher era]] |rarity=R1 |rarity_link=Rarity#Rare |uniqueness=Unique |destiny=2 |power=2 |ability=1 |deploy=1 |forfeit=0.5 |icons=[[Warrior]] |set_band=Decipher |lore=Male Rodian '''bounty hunter'''. Sent by Jabba to capture Han. Arrogant, overconfident and not too bright. Trained by bounty hunters Nataz and Goa, who betrayed him to Thuku. |game_text=During opponent's control phase, may 'threaten' one smuggler at same site. Opponent may use all Force Pile cards to cancel threat, allowing you to activate same amount. Otherwise, draw destiny. If destiny + Greedo's ability > 6, smuggler lost. |printings='''Decipher''' — [[Greedo]] (2_89)
'''Decipher (Revised)''' — '''this page''' (52_89) |sources=* [[Greedo]] black-border printed face (2_89) * White-border product [[Revised A New Hope]] * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Dark Character: Greedo, A New Hope, R1 |strategy=By Tom Landy [[Greedo]] isn't the greatest alien. In fact, nearly everybody says that his card isn't even worth space in a deck. But, in some cases, he can really be useful. At a deploy cost of one, this bounty hunter's power is two, his ability is one, his destiny is two, but his forfeit is only a half. [[Greedo]] also possesses a special ability which allows him to "threaten" Smugglers. His game text says: " During opponent's control phase, may "threaten" one smuggler at same site. Opponent may use all force pile cards to cancel "threat", allowing you to activate the same amount. Otherwise, draw destiny. If destiny plus [[Greedo]]'s ability is >6, smuggler is lost." Now I know what you are thinking. "Why would anyone use [[Greedo]]? His forfeit stinks, and to kill a smuggler, the destiny must be a six!" While all of this is true, there are always ways to improve things. For instance, to improve his forfeit, keep him around the dark side's [[Tatooine: Mos Eisley (Dark){{!}}Tatooine: Mos Eisley]]. Here, [[Greedo]]'s forfeit would get a plus one bonus, and his power would be three. Another quick way to boost his forfeit is to slap a [[Stormtrooper Utility Belt]] around his waist. [[Greedo]]'s forfeit and power would both get a plus one bonus, but if he was on the [[Death Star]], the bonus would be plus two. Now, a forfeit of two and a half isn't bad. If you have a lot of destinies of six in your deck, you will be able to "threaten" major smugglers like [[Han Solo{{!}}Han]], [[Chewbacca]], and even [[Wedge Antilles]] easily if you have certain cards that will help you. An [[Electrobinoculars]] would be ideal to locate destinies of six, if only the dark side had this device. So, use [[Reegesk]], [[Tonnika Sisters]] or any other way to steal them from your opponent. [[Electrobinoculars]] is a very popular and powerful card, so you don't have to really worry about your opponent not having them. Another good way to find destinies that you need is with [[R2-Q2 (Artoo-Kyootoo){{!}}R2-Q2]]. When at a scomp link, [[R2-Q2 (Artoo-Kyootoo){{!}}R2-Q2]] enables you to peek at the top three cards of your reserve deck during your draw phase for one force. By knowing what your destiny is, even if it isn't a six, you can still bluff because your opponent won't know if you are lying or not. [[Greedo]]'s forfeit value and special ability to "threaten" smugglers aren't great, but when combined with certain cards it can really be helpful. * [[Greeata]] * bounty hunter * Rodian }}

{{Card |title=General Veers (Revised) |versions='''Decipher''' — [[General Veers]] (3_87)
'''Decipher (Revised)''' — '''this page''' (53_87) |card_uid=53_87 |gemp_id=53_87 |image=Hoth-R-D-generalveerswb.gif |side=Dark |type=Character |subtype=Imperial |subtype_link=Imperial |set=Revised Hoth |publisher=[[Decipher]] |era=[[Decipher era]] |rarity=R1 |rarity_link=Rarity#Rare |uniqueness=Unique |destiny=1 |power=3 |ability=3 |deploy=3 |forfeit=5 |icons=[[Pilot]] [[Warrior]] |set_band=Decipher |lore=General Maximillian Veers is the model of an Imperial Army officer. Cunning, loyal and a ruthlessly efficient leader. In charge of the ground assault troops in Vader's forces. |game_text=Power +1 when at same site as Admiral Ozzel. Adds 1 to power of each Imperial at same Hoth site. Adds 3 to power of any combat vehicle he pilots. On Blizzard 1, also adds 1 to armor and draws one battle destiny if not able to otherwise. |printings='''Decipher''' — [[General Veers]] (3_87)
'''Decipher (Revised)''' — '''this page''' (53_87) |sources=* [[General Veers]] black-border printed face (3_87) * White-border product [[Revised Hoth]] * Printed face: [[General Veers]] |strategy=By Gregg Keefer, Gold 4 [[General Veers]] is one bad dude. How many people out there can face [[Darth Vader]], nose to breathing apparatus, without flinching? Aside from hispersonal charm and charisma his card is stacked with tons of useful abilitiesthat will add to your Dark Side deck and make those rebels quake with fear! For 3 Force you get 3 power and 3 ability as well as [[Red Leader{{!}}Leader]] ability. Add to that the fact that he is a Warrior and a Pilot and you have a useful, do-it-all character that works well in practically any deck strategy. But that's notall, this guy is the bomb. His pilot text carries added bonuses if you use him on combat vehicles. He adds 3 to the power of any combat vehicle which can make any Walker a nightmare to be reckoned with. Put him on the [[Imperial Walker]] from the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] 2 player game[, with its permanent pilot of ability 1, and you have 7 power and a battle destiny draw for only 7 Force. Put him on [[Blizzard 1]] and [[Veers]] commands a staggering 10 power, immunity to attrition less than 4 and a battle destiny draw all by himself ! The mighty General also adds 1 to armor on this Walker making it that much harder for those pesky Snowspeeders to take him down with their puny weapons. Bah, annoying gadflies! He's great on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] but he can really make trouble for those rebels at Cloud Sectors too. Put him on a [[Cloud Car (Dark){{!}}Cloud Car]] (a combat vehicle) at a Cloud Sector and you are looking at 6 power and a battle destiny draw for only 5 Force. Combine this with some Tibanna Gas Miners on the ground to add to your Force drain at the sector. If it's a Light Side cloud sector you're controlling you'll drain for 2, plus the Miner bonus. Nasty. He's also power plus one at the same site as that bumbling freebie [[Admiral Ozzel]] and they'll bring you 7 power (8 on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]]) plus a battle destiny for only 3 Force. Ozzel was born to be forfeited to attrition, leaving [[Veers]] to fight again another day. Should the unthinkable happen and [[Veers]] is defeated, his better than average forfeit of 5 will usually eat up even a high single destiny in attrition. General Maximillian [[Veers]]' great abilities have won him the admiration of the Empire. He is yours to command. The shield generators will be down in moments, you may start your landing. * [[Imperial Command]] * general * leader * [[General Veers]] }}

 == Editing the family navigator == This shared navigator appears in the Versions infobox of each article in the Premiere [[Darth Vader]] family. To update membership, use the '''Edit versions''' link on a member article or edit this template's source. Each publication entry uses [[Template:Card version link]] with its canonical article title and concise visible label. Use Show changes before saving, then check both the new article and existing family members. The current article highlights automatically. Add a verified publication here once and include {{Card versions/Darth Vader (Premiere)}} in its card template's versions field. Keep its existing images, text and identity. Era and set headings are linked, bold and underlined; publication entries use normal links. The PC errata of the Decipher card has its own explicitly labeled group, rather than assigning a later PC rewrite to the Decipher publishing era. This reversible Dark Side pilot covers the eleven existing family articles identified for the second test. The English Reflections foil is a known follow-up publication-inventory gap; it is not represented by an ordinary black-border image or an invented playable ID. Other Vader personas, including [[Darth Vader, Dark Lord Of The Sith]] and [[Darth Vader With Lightsaber]], belong to their own card families.
